title: Speed, distance, time
examples: How do I find the average speed if the distance changes?
What is the difference between speed and average speed?
Can you show me an example of converting minutes to hours?

explain.say: The relationship between speed, distance, and time is very important. We can remember this using a simple triangle.
If you know any two parts, you can find the third. To find speed, you divide distance by time. This gives you the rate.
If you want to find the distance, you multiply speed by time. Remember this formula for distance.
To find average speed, you must divide the total distance by the total time taken. It is not just averaging the speeds.

items: Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

draw.text: Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

explain.say: For example, if you travel ten kilometres in two hours, your average speed is five kilometres per hour.

faq.q: What is the difference between speed and average speed?
faq.a: Speed is how fast you are going at one moment. Average speed is the total distance divided by the total time for the whole journey.
asks: Is average speed the same as speed?

faq.q: How do I convert units like minutes to hours?
faq.a: There are sixty minutes in one hour. To change minutes to hours, you divide the number of minutes by sixty.
asks: How many hours in thirty minutes?

faq.q: When do I use the formula triangle?
faq.a: You use it anytime you are working with speed, distance, and time together. It helps you remember which formula to use.
asks: What is the formula triangle for?
Does the triangle help with ratios?

faq.q: If I travel at different speeds, how do I find the average speed?
faq.a: You must calculate the total distance covered and divide that by the total time taken for all parts of the trip.

faq.q: What units should I use for speed?
faq.a: Common units for speed include kilometres per hour or metres per second. The units must match the distance and time units used.
asks: What are the units for rate?

facts: Speed is calculated by dividing distance by time.
Distance travelled equals speed multiplied by time.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

quiz.say: A car travels three kilometres in one hour. What is its speed?
quiz.why: You divide the distance three by the time one, which equals three kilometres per hour.

wrong.0: This is the distance, but you need the unit of speed per hour.
wrong.1: While the calculation is correct, the answer must include the correct units.
wrong.2: This would be used to find distance, not speed.

quiz.say: A runner covers ten metres in five seconds. What is the speed?
quiz.why: You divide the distance ten by the time five, giving you two metres per second.

wrong.0: This would be the result of dividing five by ten.
wrong.1: This is just the fraction, not the final unit of measurement.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake from adding the numbers together.

quiz.say: A cyclist travels ten kilometres in two hours, and then another ten kilometres in two hours. What is the average speed?
quiz.why: The total distance is twenty kilometres, and the total time is four hours, so the average speed is five kilometres per hour.

wrong.0: This incorrectly multiplies the two speeds together.
wrong.2: This incorrectly averages the two speeds without considering the time taken for each.
wrong.3: This happens if you only divide the distance by the time of the second leg.
